newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps-Diesel slip on physical jitters.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps-Diesel slip on physical jitters.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps edged down slightly late afternoon on Wednesday on fears that the two-month long buying spree may be coming to an end, traders said.
"The market is a bit nervous and there are one or two people who are selling off their positions," one trader said.
May swaps were last quoted at $25.50/$25.60, down 15 cents from this morning and down five cents from Tuesday, brokers said.
May traded at an intra-day high of $25.57 early this afternoon before it was sold down at $25.50 and $25.45, before picking up slightly, they said.
June also fell slightly and was quoted at $24.55/$24.65, brokers said with the May/June spread traded at 98 cents.

The lower prices come despite a big increase to overnight June Brent crude values on the International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) which closed up 34 cents to $18.61 per barrel and was last traded down one cent on Wednesday.
June IPE gas oil opened firmer to last trade up $1.50 to $169.75 per tonne on top of a $2.25 gain on Tuesday.
The firmer prices in the West has virtually closed the East-West arbitrage with the curent June-June spread at $13.50 per tonne.
Industry sources said the market weakness was due to a perception based on recent trades that the traders' may soon warp up their buying spree.
On Tuesday, despite numerous players willing to sell at the traders' buying level, only two 150,000-barrel cargoes were purchased.
One at $26.20 per barrel for end May loading and another at $26.50 for mid-May loading, both on a free-on-board basis.
The traders last Thursday bought a one-day record of 2.44 million barrels, taking their tally to nearly 18 million barrels of diesel since March 3.
But despite the large purchase, physical prices have instead trekked a steady downward path from a high of about $28.75 per barrel to around $26.00 over the past two months.
Fuel oil swaps firmed in active trading May last quoted up 75 cents from Tuesday at $99.00/$99.75, brokers said. May traded earlier in the day at $99.00 and $99.15, they said.
